title: Non-contact, Label-free Monitoring of Cells and Extracellular Matrix using Raman Spectroscopy
protocol: Seed in vitro-cultured or freshly isolated adherent cells on a glass bottom dish.
Incubate the seeded cells at 37 °C and 5% CO2 until cell attachment is completed.
Remove culture medium from attached cells.
Wash cells gently three times with PBS before measurement.
Cover cells with either PBS or cell culture medium during the whole measurement procedure.
Detach in vitro-cultured suspension cells according to common protocols (e.g., trypsin-EDTA).
Centrifuge detached cells and re-suspend the obtained pellet in PBS or cell culture medium.
Transfer 100 μl of cell suspension at a concentration of up to 100,000 cells/ml to a glass bottom dish.
Transfer harvested tissues to sterile ice-cold PBS immediately after harvesting.
Store tissues no longer than 12 hours at 4 °C or on ice prior to measurement.
Cover tissues with PBS or medium during the entire measurement procedure to prevent drying.
Start the software Andor Solis and set the temperature of the CCD camera to -60 °C.
Place a silicon wafer on the microscope stage for calibration.
Turn the laser on and set the power to 85 mW.
Focus the laser onto the silicon wafer until XY appears.
Measure the silicon wafer with a single integration time of 1 sec using a 60x air objective.
Change the unit of the x-axis from pixel number to Raman shift (cm-1).
Vary the laser focus of the silicon peak at 520 cm-1 in the collected spectrum to find the maximum possible intensity for this Raman band.
Place the glass bottom dish with cells on the microscope stage.
Focus the laser on the cell nucleus, turn the microscope light off and start collecting the spectrum.
Measure a reference spectrum of the background every 10 spectra by moving the laser focus beside the cell.
Collect a new background spectrum when changing the focus depth.
Transfer 100 μl of the cell suspension into the glass bottom dish and place it onto the microscope stage.
Focus the laser on the center of the cell, turn the microscope light off and start collecting the spectrum.
Measure a reference spectrum of the background every 10 spectra by moving the laser focus beside the cell.
Collect a new background spectrum when changing the focus depth.
Place the sample into a glass bottom dish with the region of interest facing the bottom.
Fill the dish with enough PBS to cover the sample.
Place a cover glass over the sample to avoid movement during measurements.
Set the laser focus into the structure of interest.
Collect a reference spectrum of the background every 10 spectra by moving the laser focus out of the tissue area.
Collect a new background when changing the focus depth.
Section fresh, snap-frozen tissue samples using a standard cryotome.
Mount the sections on silica-coated cover glasses.
Stain the cryosections following a routine protocol for immunofluorescence.
Use only a short fixation step (maximum 10 minutes with 4% paraformaldehyde).
Employ appropriate antibodies for detecting the protein of interest.
Perform Raman measurements focusing in the area where fluorescence occurs.
Place the ventricularis side of dissected porcine aortic valve leaflets facing down in a glass bottom dish.
Measure native tissue as a 'non-incubated control' at 30 random points across the whole surface, focusing on fibrillar structures.
Divide the sample into 3 sections and place them in separate Eppendorf tubes filled with an elastase solution (5 U/ml).
Incubate the tissue for either 15 or 30 minutes at 37 °C.
Incubate the tissues for either 15 or 30 minutes.
Remove the tissues from the Eppendorf tube after incubation.
Wash the tissues carefully with PBS to stop the enzymatic reaction completely.
Measure each sample at 30 random points, focusing on fibrillar structures.
Subtract the corresponding background spectrum from the collected spectra using OPUS software (Bruker Optik GmbH/Germany) to reduce interfering signals from glass and medium.
Reduce the spectra to the wavenumber region between 400-1800 cm-1 for highest information content.
Normalize the spectra to the maximum peak if needed, to factor out intensity fluctuations and systematic failures.
Perform a baseline correction to increase comparability between different experiments.
Label each group of measurements by creating row ranges for every sample group.
Use the following basic settings for the PCA: cross-validation, the NIPALS algorithm, no rotation.
Start the PCA analysis.
Use cells in suspension for Raman spectroscopic analysis.
Measure the mean Raman spectra and standard deviations of human fibroblasts, mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs), chondrocytes, and keratinocytes in suspension.
Analyze the spectral region between 600 and 1800 cm-1 for clear differences between cell types.
